criteria.text: `test/fixture.ts` gains a `wikipedia` field on at least one fixture person and a helper to seed `person_attention` rows (or an inline insert in the new test file); `GET /api/people/:id/attention?days=30` against that fixture returns the seeded `{ day, views }` rows ordered ascending by day.
A person outside the requested `days` window is excluded: a row seeded 40 days ago is absent from a `?days=30` response and present at `?days=365`.
A tracked person with no `wikipedia` field and no `person_attention` rows returns `{ days: 30, series: [] }` with HTTP 200, not 404 and not an error.
`GET /api/people/does-not-exist/attention` returns 404 with `{ error: 'person not found' }`, the same shape `test/graph.test.ts` (or its sibling) already pins for other `:id` routes.
`?days=45` snaps to 30 (nearest of `[7, 30, 365]`, tie rule per existing `snapDays` behaviour) — asserted directly against `parseAttentionQuery`/`snapDays`, not by re-deriving the tie table.

Writing a `person_attention` row for `(person_id, day)` that already exists with a different `views` value updates it in place (`on conflict ... do update`), never producing a second row and never leaving the old value — a test inserts, re-inserts the same day with a different count, and asserts one row with the new count.

Removing a person from the seed list (the existing `pruneRemoved` path) deletes that person's `person_attention` rows via the FK's `on delete cascade`, verified the same way `test/store.test.ts` (or wherever `pruneRemoved` is already tested) checks `doc_persons`/`doc_testimony` cleanup — no new orphan-row code needed.

The pageviews collector test drives its HTTP call entirely through `test/effect.ts`'s stub `fetch`/`FetchHttpClient.Fetch`/`TestClock` harness (per `test/collectors-camara.test.ts`'s pattern) — no real network call, and a 429/5xx response exercises the retry-and-backoff path under `TestClock`, never a real `sleep`.

A person whose stub-fetch call resolves 404 (or any non-2xx) is skipped: that person contributes zero rows, and a sibling person in the same run still gets theirs written — the per-person isolation from the SQL/logic section, exercised at the collector level.

A failure at the ingest stage's own SQL write (not a fetch failure) surfaces as `IngestFailure({ stage: 'pageviews' })` — driven by `test/ingest.test.ts`'s `failingSql` pattern matched to the new stage's own statement, mirroring how the existing stages are each pinned there.

`src/graph.ts`'s new `attentionQuery` builder has its rendered SQL text pinned via the `statements`-export pattern the module doc describes for every other builder — a test asserts the text, not just a live execution.

`docs/api.md` names `/api/people/:id/attention`, its `days` parameter and default, and the `{ days, series }` shape with `{ day, views }` rows — checked against `docsText` (every page at once) per `test/docs.ts`, not against one file's heading or wording.

`docs/sources.md`/the source table gains no new collector row for `pageviews` and `test/docs-drift.test.ts` continues to pass unchanged — pageviews is not a `Collector`, produces no `RawDoc`, and must not appear in `defaultSources` or the `source`/`kind` filter documentation. State this as a non-criterion already covered: no new test is written for it.
`pnpm typecheck` passes with `Person.wikipedia?: string` added and `Source`/`RawDoc`/`Collector`/`CollectorError` in `src/types.ts` left untouched — a diff review criterion, not a runtime one.
